item.text: {"question_id":"4B.8","answer":"During the 2023 target period, López Obrador complied formally with the constitutional six-year, nonreelection rule: he could not seek reelection, and succession remained scheduled through the constitutional 2024 election framework. However, his conduct toward broader transfer safeguards was mixed. He personally sought to shape the next administration by directing Morena’s succession process, favoring Claudia Sheinbaum, proposing arrangements for primary runners-up, and promoting policies intended to extend his influence after leaving office (BATCH-0031-E004; BATCH-0028-E006). Morena aspirants’ early campaign activity also escaped the normal fiscalization process, although the evidence does not establish that López Obrador personally ordered or was legally responsible for each expenditure (BATCH-0026-E009). His proposed electoral reforms would have enabled presidential and ruling-party influence over electoral-authority appointments, reduced the electoral authority’s budget, and eliminated local authorities; the fallback Plan B was later suspended and invalidated through judicial and electoral-institutional review (BATCH-0042-E006; BATCH-0043-E010; BATCH-0013-E016; BATCH-0014-E005). Electoral institutions nevertheless continued to function: the INE administered and certified the 2022 recall process under constitutional rules, and the electoral tribunal unanimously upheld an opposition gubernatorial victory after Morena’s challenge (BATCH-0029-E008; BATCH-0030-E010). Thus, the evidence supports formal compliance with the presidential term limit and functioning institutional checks, but not unqualified respect for neutral succession conditions or institutional safeguards against continued political influence. The 2023 record does not directly establish whether López Obrador personally obstructed the eventual 2024 transfer, and the supplied evidence does not prove that the reforms were designed specifically to evade his own term limit. Earlier disputes over the 2006 and 2012 elections are historical context only and should not be treated as direct evidence of 2023 succession conduct (BATCH-0024-E004;
